name: microplan-to-opp
narrative: Maya opens her program's microplan workspace, where candidate plans live and are tuned long before any Connect opportunity goes live. She turns an administrative district into a draft plan — the work-area grid is generated from the boundary, not drawn by hand. The grid then balances itself across her named field workers, so no one is handed a sprawling territory while someone else gets a tight one. Maya and her local partner walk the plan on the review page, dropping the squares that aren't real settlements and reassigning a worker, and the per-worker travel and workload numbers move as they edit. Once it reads right, she walks the plan through its lifecycle — Submit for review, then Approve. She deploys the approved plan by binding it to the live Connect opportunity it will run under, then downloads the work areas in Connect's own import format, field-for-field — ready to hand to the opportunity. The plan is designed, validated, approved, and exported, all in the planning phase before Connect runs a thing.

maya.intro: Maya designs and validates field-worker microplans for her program with a local partner, then hands the finished plan to the Connect opportunity that will run it.
maya.name: Maya Okonkwo

features.description: Program workspace at /microplans/program/<id>/ listing candidate plans grouped by lifecycle phase (Planning vs Live)
features.verify: Playwright: load /microplans/program/133/, assert a Planning column and a Live column each render plan cards with a status badge

scenes.title: The workspace before any opportunity exists

features.description: Admin-boundary picker on the plan setup page that resolves a district to a polygon
features.verify: pytest: POST to the create-plan endpoint with a boundary id returns a plan whose area geometry is the selected district

features.description: Coverage grid generation that materializes one work area per grid cell inside the boundary
features.verify: pytest: a generated coverage plan has work_areas length > 0 each tagged with the source boundary

scenes.title: Maya turns a district into a draft plan

features.description: Two-phase group (bbox or BFS-adjacency) then assign (round-robin or Neal-Lesh minimax spread) over the work areas, run on Celery
features.verify: pytest: assigning a plan leaves every non-excluded work area with a work_area_group and an assignee

scenes.title: The grid balances itself across field workers

features.description: Review page work-area list with exclude / regroup / reassign controls that append a planning-phase audit event in Connect's pghistory field shape
features.verify: pytest: excluding a work area sets its status to EXCLUDED and appends a planning-phase audit event for that area

features.description: Per-field-worker metrics table (areas, workload, travel) that recomputes after an edit without a full page reload
features.verify: Playwright: exclude a work area on the review page and assert the metrics table row totals change

scenes.title: Maya reads the per-worker numbers with the partner

features.description: Plan transition endpoint enforcing the allowed Draft to In review to Approved moves and logging each with actor and timestamp
features.verify: pytest: POST transition draft to in_review then in_review to approved succeeds and each appends a status_log entry; an illegal jump returns 400

scenes.title: Maya walks the plan to Approved

features.description: Deploy opens a searchable picker of the owner's live opportunities; choosing one binds its opportunity_id and sets status to deployed (terminal in labs)
features.verify: pytest: transition approved to deployed without an opportunity_id raises ValueError; with one, plan.opportunity_id is set and status is deployed

scenes.title: Maya binds the plan to a live opportunity

features.description: CSV export of non-excluded work areas in the exact column order of Connect's WorkAreaCSVImporter headers, with LGA/State populated so it imports without edits
features.verify: pytest: the exported CSV header row equals WorkAreaCSVImporter.HEADERS, one row per non-excluded work area, and LGA/State are non-empty

scenes.title: The plan leaves in Connect's own format
